chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who arrived from a journey during the month of Ramadan and had not tasted anything before midday (zawal). He said, 'He fasts.'
These two reports indicate that whenever he had not eaten anything and arrived before midday, it is obligatory upon him to fast that day.
And that which indicates that when the dawn rises and he is outside the town, he has the choice, is what has been narrated:

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: Midday, the time when the sun begins to decline from its zenith
key_terms.يَصُومُ: He fasts (indicating obligation in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler arriving home during Ramadan before midday?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi cites this narration to clarify the juristic debate regarding a traveler's obligation upon returning home during Ramadan. The ruling hinges on whether the traveler has consumed anything before midday (*zawal*); if not, fasting is immediately obligatory, whereas arriving after dawn grants them the choice (*ikhtiyar*) to continue or break the fast. This distinction highlights the Shia emphasis on the precise timing of the traveler's status change relative to the daily fasting window.
